title: Implementation Evidence Loop
summary: Implement coding-agent changes in small increments that continuously prove scope, behavior, safety, and recoverability.

sections.title: Use the smallest useful evidence loop
paragraphs: For each plan step, inspect the relevant contract and existing tests, make one coherent change, run the narrowest meaningful check, inspect the diff, and then run the broader affected suite. Record observed results rather than claiming success from code appearance. Keep unrelated user changes intact.

When a check fails, classify whether the defect is in the implementation, test, environment, dependency, or assumption. Fix the cause, rerun the failing check, and retain enough output for reproduction. Do not weaken assertions or delete safeguards merely to obtain a green result.

This worked exercise uses only local Python 3 standard-library features. It has no database, network request, production data, package download, secret, remote write, or destructive command. All correctness claims are independently testable without a paid account.

sections.title: Record each implementation increment
paragraphs: Evidence should connect the requested criterion to the changed artifact and to a reproducible observation. Redact sensitive output and summarize large logs while preserving the exact command, version, failure signature, and result.
Use this reusable template after reading the filled example. Expected results state the oracle before execution. Observed results must come from the process that actually ran the command.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a chain from acceptance criterion to changed files, narrow verification, affected-suite verification, diff inspection, safety check, and recovery path. A passing check without that trace is incomplete evidence.

Before handoff, reproduce the main user journey from an isolated checkout, compare the final diff with the approved plan, scan for credentials and generated noise, and list any untested behavior. Require independent review when consequence, security sensitivity, or repository policy warrants it.
NIST Secure Software Development Framework guidance is the first-party security reference for the evidence-loop context: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/218/final

sections.title: Worked case: state the contract before changing code
paragraphs: The synthetic service starts with five units of stock. A validated reservation request contains a nonempty string request ID, a nonempty string item, and a positive integer quantity. Python bool values are not quantities even though bool is a subclass of int. Floating-point values, NaN, fractions, zero, negative values, and quantities greater than available stock are invalid.

A successful first request moves its quantity from available stock to reserved stock. Independent accounting requires reserved to equal the sum of quantities in reservation records, reserved and available to remain nonnegative integers, and that record sum plus available equal total stock.

A request ID is bound to the validated Python payload tuple `(item, quantity)`. This is exact equality for the two validated values. It is not a claim of byte-for-byte serialized equivalence. Reusing the ID with either value changed raises RequestConflict before mutation. Reusing it with the same payload returns the original reservation without changing stock.

In this fixture, an unknown outcome means the reservation is committed locally and then UnknownOutcome is raised before the caller receives the result. Replaying the same request reconciles the committed operation without reserving again.

Malformed input, invalid quantity, and over-reservation are rejected before mutation. A snapshot copies reserved stock and the request map; restore replaces both, providing a local recovery path without external side effects.
sections.callout: Decision trace: conservation -> compare the sum of reservation records with stored reserved stock and available stock; exact binding -> validate strict types and compare item plus quantity; unknown outcome -> commit before raising and reconcile through the stored request; denial safety -> compare snapshots before and after rejection; recovery -> restore both pieces of mutable state.

sections.title: Seven baseline tests that expose the defect
paragraphs: Save this complete file as test_buggy_inventory.py. Exactly seven test methods are defined. Under the supplied fixture, the shallow first-reservation and ordinary invalid-quantity tests are expected to pass. Replay, changed-payload, bool, fractional, and empty-ID tests are expected to fail.
The expected summary is 7 tests run with 5 failures and a nonzero process exit. This is a reasoned test oracle, not an observed run. Preserve the actual output even if it differs.

code.label: test_buggy_inventory.py
code.code:
import json
import unittest

from buggy_inventory import Inventory, RequestConflict, UnknownOutcome


with open("fixture.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    FIXTURE = json.load(handle)


class BuggyInventoryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_first_reservation_has_expected_fixture_values(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        result = inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        quantity = FIXTURE["request"]["quantity"]
        self.assertEqual(result.quantity, quantity)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.available, FIXTURE["total_stock"] - quantity)

    def test_unknown_outcome_replay_does_not_double_reserve(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        with self.assertRaises(UnknownOutcome):
            inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"], simulate_unknown=True)
        inventory.replay(**FIXTURE["request"])
        quantity = FIXTURE["request"]["quantity"]
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, quantity)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.available, FIXTURE["total_stock"] - quantity)

    def test_same_id_with_changed_payload_is_rejected(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        changed = dict(FIXTURE["request"])
        changed["quantity"] = 1
        with self.assertRaises(RequestConflict):
            inventory.reserve(**changed)

    def test_zero_negative_and_excessive_quantities_are_rejected(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        for request in [
            ("zero", "blue-pencil", 0),
            ("negative", "blue-pencil", -1),
            ("excess", "blue-pencil", FIXTURE["total_stock"] + 1),
        ]:
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                inventory.reserve(*request)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, 0)

    def test_bool_quantity_is_rejected(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            inventory.reserve("bool", "blue-pencil", True)

    def test_fractional_quantity_is_rejected(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            inventory.reserve("fraction", "blue-pencil", 1.5)

    def test_empty_request_id_is_rejected(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            inventory.reserve("", "blue-pencil", 1)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

sections.title: After code: make the smallest coherent correction
paragraphs: Save this complete corrected implementation as inventory.py. Validation occurs before request lookup or mutation. A prior request is returned only when its validated item and quantity equal the new validated payload. State is committed before an optional UnknownOutcome is raised.

The implementation keeps available as a derived property, but the tests do not rely on the algebraic expression alone. They independently sum reservation records and compare that sum with reserved stock before checking conservation.

code.label: inventory.py

sections.title: Correct tests, independent oracles, negative cases, and recovery
paragraphs: Save this complete file as test_inventory.py. All fixture-dependent assertions derive their quantities and expected availability from fixture.json, so the changed-input task does not require hardcoded assertion edits.

The accounting helper first verifies that all recorded quantities are strict integers, sums the records independently, compares the sum with stored reserved stock, checks nonnegative integer state, and only then checks total conservation. This avoids treating `reserved + (total - reserved) == total` as sufficient evidence.

Denial tests compare a complete snapshot before and after each malformed, invalid, excessive, or conflicting request. They cover bool, NaN, fractional quantity, wrong metadata types, empty strings, and a non-bool simulation flag.

code.label: test_inventory.py
code.code:
import json
import math
import unittest

from inventory import Inventory, RequestConflict, UnknownOutcome


with open("fixture.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
    FIXTURE = json.load(handle)


class InventoryTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def assert_accounting(self, inventory):
        records = list(inventory.requests.values())
        self.assertTrue(all(type(record.quantity) is int for record in records))
        recorded_quantity = sum(record.quantity for record in records)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, recorded_quantity)
        self.assertIs(type(inventory.reserved), int)
        self.assertIs(type(inventory.available), int)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(inventory.reserved, 0)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(inventory.available, 0)
        self.assertEqual(recorded_quantity + inventory.available, inventory.total_stock)

    def assert_denied_without_mutation(self, inventory, exception, *args, **kwargs):
        before = inventory.snapshot()
        with self.assertRaises(exception):
            inventory.reserve(*args, **kwargs)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.snapshot(), before)
        self.assert_accounting(inventory)

    def test_first_reservation_uses_fixture_values(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        result = inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        request = FIXTURE["request"]
        self.assertEqual(result.request_id, request["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(result.item, request["item"])
        self.assertEqual(result.quantity, request["quantity"])
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, request["quantity"])
        self.assertEqual(
            inventory.available,
            FIXTURE["total_stock"] - request["quantity"],
        )
        self.assert_accounting(inventory)

    def test_unknown_outcome_reconciles_by_replay(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        with self.assertRaises(UnknownOutcome):
            inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"], simulate_unknown=True)
        after_commit = inventory.snapshot()
        result = inventory.replay(**FIXTURE["request"])
        self.assertEqual(inventory.snapshot(), after_commit)
        self.assertEqual(result.quantity, FIXTURE["request"]["quantity"])
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, FIXTURE["request"]["quantity"])
        self.assertEqual(
            inventory.available,
            FIXTURE["total_stock"] - FIXTURE["request"]["quantity"],
        )
        self.assert_accounting(inventory)

    def test_same_payload_retry_is_idempotent(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        first = inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        after_first = inventory.snapshot()
        second = inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.snapshot(), after_first)
        self.assert_accounting(inventory)

    def test_changed_item_or_quantity_conflicts_without_mutation(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        request = FIXTURE["request"]
        self.assert_denied_without_mutation(
            inventory,
            RequestConflict,
            request["request_id"],
            request["item"] + "-changed",
            request["quantity"],
        )
        changed_quantity = 1 if request["quantity"] != 1 else 2
        self.assert_denied_without_mutation(
            inventory,
            RequestConflict,
            request["request_id"],
            request["item"],
            changed_quantity,
        )

    def test_invalid_excessive_and_non_integer_quantities_are_denied(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        invalid = [
            (ValueError, "zero", 0),
            (ValueError, "negative", -1),
            (ValueError, "excess", FIXTURE["total_stock"] + 1),
            (TypeError, "true", True),
            (TypeError, "false", False),
            (TypeError, "fraction", 1.5),
            (TypeError, "nan", math.nan),
        ]
        for exception, request_id, quantity in invalid:
            with self.subTest(request_id=request_id):
                self.assert_denied_without_mutation(
                    inventory,
                    exception,
                    request_id,
                    "blue-pencil",
                    quantity,
                )

    def test_malformed_metadata_is_denied_before_mutation(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        cases = [
            (ValueError, ("", "item", 1), {}),
            (TypeError, (7, "item", 1), {}),
            (ValueError, ("r-empty-item", "", 1), {}),
            (TypeError, ("r-bad-item", 7, 1), {}),
            (TypeError, ("r-bad-flag", "item", 1), {"simulate_unknown": 1}),
        ]
        for exception, args, kwargs in cases:
            with self.subTest(args=args, kwargs=kwargs):
                self.assert_denied_without_mutation(
                    inventory,
                    exception,
                    *args,
                    **kwargs,
                )

    def test_snapshot_restore_is_recovery_path(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        before = inventory.snapshot()
        inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        self.assertNotEqual(inventory.snapshot(), before)
        inventory.restore(before)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.snapshot(), before)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, 0)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.available, FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        self.assert_accounting(inventory)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import unittest

from wrong_fix import Inventory, RequestConflict


class IndependentRequestBindingTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_changed_payload_with_same_id_is_rejected(self):
        inventory = Inventory(5)
        inventory.reserve("r", "item", 2)
        before = (inventory.reserved, inventory.available, dict(inventory.requests))
        with self.assertRaises(RequestConflict):
            inventory.reserve("r", "item", 1)
        after = (inventory.reserved, inventory.available, dict(inventory.requests))
        self.assertEqual(after, before)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

sections.title: Bind observed results to runtime file hashes
paragraphs: Save this complete recorder as evidence.py. It computes SHA-256 hashes at runtime, launches the corrected test command as a subprocess, captures the actual exit code, stdout, and stderr, and writes the JSON record even when tests fail. Python documents hashlib and SHA-256 support at https://docs.python.org/3/library/hashlib.html

The recorder exits with the test subprocess status after preserving the record. Therefore a failed test does not become a successful validation merely because evidence.json was written. When `--compare` names an earlier record, `stale` is true if any bound file hash differs.

sections.title: Exact commands, rerun, stale-result check, and rollback evidence
paragraphs: Save every file under its displayed filename in one isolated directory. Use explicit test module names because the directory intentionally contains tests that should fail. `python3 --version` records the interpreter. If a local system documents `python` as its Python 3 command, substitute it consistently.

The baseline command is expected to exit nonzero after seven tests with five failures. Preserve that output. The corrected command is expected to pass seven tests. The evidence command reruns the corrected tests itself and records their actual result. Its process exits nonzero if those tests fail, even though it preserves the JSON.

Rollback evidence is included in the corrected suite. The recovery test snapshots empty state, reserves the fixture quantity, restores the snapshot, and verifies the request records, reserved stock, available stock, strict integer state, and conservation.

sections.title: Classify execution failures versus product defects
paragraphs: An execution failure means verification did not reach the intended assertion. Examples include a missing file, syntax error in the harness, unavailable Python command, permission error, or wrong working directory. It is evidence about the procedure or environment, not proof that the inventory contract is wrong.

A product defect means the intended test ran and observed behavior violated the contract. Examples are reserved stock becoming 4 after reserving quantity 2 and replaying it, accepting a changed quantity for the same request ID, or mutating state after rejecting malformed input.

Preserve both kinds of failure. Record the command, Python version, exit status, stdout, stderr, and failure signature. Repair an execution failure before drawing a product conclusion. Repair a product defect while retaining its regression test. If classification remains uncertain, record UNKNOWN and identify the next discriminating check.
sections.callout: A written evidence file is not proof of success. Read the recorded child exit code and observed label, and reject stale evidence after any bound file changes.

sections.title: Changed-input learner task
paragraphs: Change only `fixture.json` request quantity from 2 to 3. Do not edit inventory.py or test_inventory.py. The fixture-driven tests must adapt without hardcoded expected values.

Trace the decision before editing: requested quantity changes from 2 to 3; first reservation must produce reserved 3 and available 2; replay must preserve reserved 3 and available 2; total stock remains 5; exact request binding and all negative cases remain unchanged; the fixture hash changes, so evidence.json from before the edit is stale.

Run `python3 -m unittest -v test_inventory.py`, then run `python3 evidence.py --record evidence-after-change.json --compare evidence.json`. Expected results are seven passing tests, recorder test exit 0, and stale true. These are expected outcomes, not claims of actual execution.

        ]
        for exception, request_id, quantity in invalid:
            with self.subTest(request_id=request_id):
                self.assert_denied_without_mutation(
                    inventory,
                    exception,
                    request_id,
                    "blue-pencil",
                    quantity,
                )

    def test_malformed_metadata_is_denied_before_mutation(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        cases = [
            (ValueError, ("", "item", 1), {}),
            (TypeError, (7, "item", 1), {}),
            (ValueError, ("r-empty-item", "", 1), {}),
            (TypeError, ("r-bad-item", 7, 1), {}),
            (TypeError, ("r-bad-flag", "item", 1), {"simulate_unknown": 1}),
        ]
        for exception, args, kwargs in cases:
            with self.subTest(args=args, kwargs=kwargs):
                self.assert_denied_without_mutation(
                    inventory,
                    exception,
                    *args,
                    **kwargs,
                )

    def test_snapshot_restore_is_recovery_path(self):
        inventory = Inventory(FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        before = inventory.snapshot()
        inventory.reserve(**FIXTURE["request"])
        self.assertNotEqual(inventory.snapshot(), before)
        inventory.restore(before)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.snapshot(), before)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.reserved, 0)
        self.assertEqual(inventory.available, FIXTURE["total_stock"])
        self.assert_accounting(inventory)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

sections.title: Changed-input answer and actionable feedback
paragraphs: Complete expected answer: fixture quantity is 3; inventory.py and the fixture-driven test file are unchanged; first reservation is reserved 3 and available 2; unknown-outcome replay remains reserved 3 and available 2; the independent conservation result is 3 plus 2 equals 5.

If the corrected tests report `3 != 2`, inspect test_inventory.py for a hardcoded quantity or availability assertion and restore the complete fixture-driven solution above. If availability is 1, inspect whether the operation reserved twice or the fixture was accidentally changed to 4. If a changed payload is accepted, compare both item and quantity before returning a prior result.

If the comparison reports stale false, confirm that the earlier evidence.json was created before the fixture edit, that fixture.json is in BOUND_FILES, and that `--compare evidence.json` names the pre-edit record. If the recorder exits nonzero, inspect its recorded child exit code, stdout, and stderr rather than treating the existence of the JSON file as success.

If Python cannot start, a file cannot be imported, or the working directory is wrong, classify that as an execution failure. Preserve the message, repair the procedure, and rerun before evaluating product behavior.

sections.title: Transfer the method across model families and coding agents
paragraphs: The evidence loop is provider-neutral. A practitioner can ask any permitted coding agent to inspect the contract, propose one bounded change, run the exact local command, inspect the diff, and return the hash-bound evidence. The contract and independently runnable tests remain the authority.

Optional model families include Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, and Z.ai, as well as families from other providers. Tool use, local execution, context limits, sandboxing, approvals, and filesystem permissions are deployment-specific. A family name does not establish any of those capabilities.

The exercise itself requires no vendor account or vendor-specific behavior. If an agent cannot execute locally, a human can run the same standard-library commands and supply the observed evidence. Compare systems by traceability and correctness, not assumed vendor features.
sections.callout: Keep the contract, independent oracle, negative cases, failure classification, runtime hash binding, stale-result check, and recovery test. Change only the deployment-specific interface after checking its documented permissions.
